image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: Ebola: Africa CDC plans to use vaccine for different strain as outbreak spreads
item.description: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control pledged to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain in the current DRC outbreak, with test cases indicating a potentially live-saving level of protection.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How drought threatens electricity supplies in Europe
item.description: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Can UN chief's initiative kickstart resolution for Cyprus?
item.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres considers a resolution to the Cyprus issue to be vital for regional stability and has initiated a new diplomatic effort. What are the prospects for its success?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Iran is sending mixed signals on talks
item.description: Trump says talks with Iran are underway. Tehran says it is discussing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, not Washington. Analysts say the gap reflects competing political pressures.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Africa and the ICC: Why most countries are staying
item.description: A new wave of African withdrawals has swept through the International Criminal Court. Chad turned its back on the court after three junta-led states in the Sahel exited. But most African countries still trust The Hague.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What's behind the Algeria-Morocco rivalry?
item.description: Morocco and Algeria have been at odds for decades, chiefly over the territory of Western Sahara. But their rivalry now extends far beyond the territory.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hiroshima survivors warn against Japan's rearmament
item.description: On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Will Russia start a fresh mobilization drive?
item.description: Russia is preparing a new mobilization campaign to boost troop numbers, Ukrainian officials and independent Russian media outlets report. The Kremlin denies this.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: WHO's Tedros visits DR Congo as Ebola outbreak accelerates
item.description: The head of the World Health Organization warned that "we must urgently and massively scale up all our efforts" against the latest Ebola outbreak, with new cases doubling in some hotspots in the past week alone.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Fears of renewed conflict in Ethiopia
item.description: Military activity in and around the disputed city of Alamata has sparked concerns that the fragile peace that followed the 2020–2022 Tigray War could unravel.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India's Gen Z protest enters a new online battle
item.description: The streets are quiet, but a fight over the legacy of the Cockroach Janta Party movement is intensifying across Instagram, memes and social media.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hungary's Lake Velence is drying up
item.description: Hungary is feeling the heat. The country's third-largest lake is shrinking, the Danube is running low, and soaring temperatures could force the country's only nuclear power plant to shut down.
